target_customer: Young mobile users who watch, vote on and perform in live talent shows, funded by advertising or sponsors
problem: Reality TV and talent shows were not interactive on mobile, so viewers could not take part or be featured live.
business_model: Consumer app with live shows, planned monetization through sponsors and ads (not confirmed)
product_category: Consumer entertainment, live interactive mobile show

founders.name: Alexandra Botez
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2018-07-25) says her interest came from live streaming her chess games on Twitch.

founders.name: Ruben Mayer-Hirshfeld
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch names him as CTO with no further background.

competitors.name: HQ Trivia
competitors.what: Live mobile game show app with cash prizes
competitors.traction_then: More than 1 million live viewers daily
competitors.funding_then: $15M at $100M post money led by Founders Fund (2018-03)

competitors.name: Musical.ly
competitors.what: Short video app named by TechCrunch as a comparison and as a platform that would struggle to build this experience

technical_complexity.rationale: Live video, voting and daily live shows at scale need real time infrastructure, which is moderately hard for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Format and app were easy to copy, and the product relied on constant content and audience acquisition.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HQ Trivia itself later shut down; no evidence incumbents copied FameGame.

market_need_then: Live mobile shows like HQ Trivia drew millions in early 2018, showing appetite for appointment viewing on phones, but the fit for talent contests was untested.

branding.domain_note: The YC website field links to an App Store page, so no own domain was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as reality TV for mobile, a mix of American Idol, Musical.ly and HQ Trivia

branding.brand_signature: Daily live show at 5 PM PT hosted with shoutouts to users
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch at launch; no fan or meme evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name and a TechCrunch feature, but no evidence of a lasting audience.

outcome_analysis: FameGame launched a live talent show app in 2018 and was covered by TechCrunch after joining YC in Summer 2018. The YC page lists it inactive, but no shutdown notice, date or cause was found. The category of live mobile game shows collapsed when HQ Trivia ended, yet that is not evidence for FameGame, so no failure factors are assigned. The cause is not public.
notes: The App Store page fetch redirected and was not followed; it is treated as the only product site. Funding: an aggregator snippet cited a $650K seed with a 2012 date and $1.4M total, and a Loot Drop page cites $3.0M burned, but the attribution to this company was unclear and the date impossible, so no round was recorded; unverified. The YC page links a Crunchbase slug that does not match the company. Outcome search found no shutdown report. Founder education and prior employers not found.
